predecessors.name: Roman Kingdom
predecessors.text: the ager Romanus, 'not beyond 15 miles from the city', from the expulsion of the Tarquins in 509 BC

successors.name: Roman Empire
successors.text: the whole Republic, Italy, the provinces and the client kingdoms, with Cyprus, Cilicia Aspera and Egypt (Octavian's holdings of 31-30), as Augustus took them in January 27 BC

ledger.x: 509 BC: the Tarquins expelled; Brutus and Collatinus the first consuls.
377 BC: Antium taken from the Volsci.
328 BC: a colony at Fregellae on the Liris, which the Samnites regarded as theirs and 'later took'; the Liris had been the line between the Roman and Samnite spheres since the treaty of 354.
304 BC: 'the ancient treaty was restored'; Bovianum had fallen in 305.

304 BC: the Marsi, Marrucini, Paeligni and Frentani become Rome's allies ('socii'), the Vestini in 302; allied by treaty, supplying troops under Roman command: the lighter tint of rule 4 until the Social War.
ledger.cp: Marsi, Marrucini, Paeligni, Frentani and Vestini (Italian allies)

ledger.x: 299 BC: a treaty with the Picentes.

299 BC: 'When in 299 BC the Romans captured Nequinum, they also concluded a treaty with the Picentes'; the Umbri page: 'The Romans first made contact with Umbria in 310 BC and settled Latin colonies there in 299 BC, 268 BC and 241 BC'.
290 BC: the Samnites 'subjugated in 290 BC' become Roman allies; Samnium is tint, not colour, until the Social War, when the Samnites and Lucanians rebel (91).
290 BC: 'the consuls mopped up remaining resistance'; the Samnite Wars give Rome 'control of a large part of central-southern Italy'.
280 BC: Locri and other allies defect after Heraclea; the shape of 279 retreats on the Bruttian coast.
272 BC (campaigns 275-272): the Lucanians and Bruttians 'reduced to subjection in a ten-year campaign (272)' after Pyrrhus' departure (Beneventum 275); allies by treaty (tint).
272 BC: the Italiote Greek cities become allies.
272 BC: Tarentum taken; Pyrrhus 'died at Argos later that year'.
268 BC: the Picentes' treaty status ends with annexation; Ancona and Asculum stay allied cities.
267 BC: 'In 267 BC, Rome conquered the Messapii and Brundisium.'
264 BC: the remaining Etruscan cities (Tarquinii, Arretium, Perusia, Volaterrae, Clusium...) as Roman allies; the Umbri's conquest was complete 'by approximately 260 BC'.

c. 260 BC: 'They had completed their conquest of Umbria by approximately 260 BC'. The Umbrian cities are allies until the citizenship of 90; umbri.json books the conquest as a loss and dissolve in 260, the same modelling difference as for…
257 BC: the Mamertines pass out of the record; Cliopatria ends their row here and the Mamertines page says they 'were lost to the historical record' once the Punic Wars overtook them.

255 BC: Xanthippus defeats Regulus at Tunis: 'About 2,000 retreated to Aspis, 500 (including Regulus) were captured'; the evacuation fleet won at Cape Hermaeum and was wrecked by a storm; the map caption has the Romans leaving Africa in 254.
252 BC: the last Carthaginian hold-outs west of Palermo.
241 BC: Catulus and Falto defeat the Carthaginian fleet at the Aegates Islands; peace.

c. 238 BC: the Veneti 'established amicitia with Rome against the Gauls c. 238 BC'; friendship rather than subjection, drawn as tint because the Veneti fought beside Rome at Telamon and passed into Roman Italy without a conquest. eu-03-b-fix 2026-10-19: the Cenomani page was opened; it says 'Rome won…
238 BC: 'Rome's first campaigns against the Ligures fell in the 230s BC' and 'Ti.

ledger.cp: Greek cities of the Illyrian coast (Epidamnos, Apollonia, Corcyra, Issa)

ledger.x: 225-222 BC: the Gallic war in the Po valley.
222 BC: the Insubres surrender; colonies at Placentia and Cremona follow.

ledger.cp: Illyrian towns under Roman protection (Pharos, Dimale)

ledger.x: 218 BC: Cisalpine Gaul rises for Hannibal.
218 BC: the Boii's submission of 225 ends with their alliance with Hannibal; Silva Litana (216) destroys Postumius' army.
218 BC (November): the Insubres go over to Hannibal.
216 BC: Capua and the south go over to Hannibal after Cannae (August 216).
215 BC: Syracuse leaves the Roman alliance.
213-212 BC: Philip takes the protectorate's interior.
ledger.cp: Illyrian towns under Roman protection (Pharos, Dimale)

ledger.x: 212 BC: the same land as the line above, the mirror of antigonid-dynasty's gain.
209 BC: Tarentum 'recaptured by treachery in 209 BC'.
206 BC: Ilipa; Carthage expelled from Iberia.
205 BC: the Roman protectorate over those places is restored; it ends in the province of Macedonia in 148 (the vassal_end below).
ledger.cp: Illyrian towns under Roman protection (Pharos, Dimale)

ledger.x: 205 BC: 'The Peace of Phoenice (205 BC) formally ended the war.'

203 BC: the Samnite, Lucanian and Bruttian rebels return to Rome's allegiance as Hannibal, who 'withdrew' to Bruttium, is recalled to Africa; the Second Punic War page gives no city-by-city dates for the south after Tarentum (209) and Locri (defected 215).
200 BC: the Second Macedonian War, infobox 'March 200 - June 197 BC'; the same zone as antigonid-dynasty.json /ledger/53.
June 197 BC: Cynoscephalae; infobox result 'Roman coalition victory'; 'Philip had to remove all his garrisons in Greek cities in Europe and Asia, which were to be free and autonomous'.

196-194 BC: the garrisons in Chalcis and Demetrias, 'cities which had belonged to Macedon'; the Isthmian proclamation was at 'the Isthmian Games of May 196 BC'. antigonid-dynasty.json /ledger/58 books the three cities as a 196 loss (Corinth included); Corinth is the Achaean line above, so only Chalcis and Demetrias…
196 BC: 'At the end of Second Macedonian War in 196 BCE, Rome established Thessaly as a koinon'; Flamininus' decree left the peoples 'free, without garrisons and subject to no tribute'.
194 BC: 'the legions were not completely evacuated until 194 BC'.
189 BC: 'The consul of 189 BC, Marcus Fulvius Nobilior... later in the year negotiated a final peace with both the Aetolians and the Cephallenians'; Ambracia besieged the same year.
189 BC: 'Aetolia also was reduced to a Roman client state'; the Aetolian League page dates the client state to 188.
179 BC: Gracchus' settlement ends the war; the Celtiberians stay outside the provinces until Numantia.
171-168 BC: the Third Macedonian War against Perseus.
168 BC: Gentius defeated 'at Scodra by a Roman force under L.
ledger.cp: Illyria (the three cantons of Gentius' kingdom)

ledger.x: 168 BC: 'Leucas was separated from Acarnania, and the city of Thyrreion was appointed the new capital'.
155 BC: 'Sporadic mountain fighting continued until M.
154/153-133 BC: the Celtiberian and Numantine wars.
148 BC: the merides end in the province.
148 BC: the Illyrian protectorates pass into the province, whose northern border starts 'from Lissus on the Adriatic'.
ledger.cp: Greek cities of the Illyrian coast (Epidamnos, Apollonia, Corcyra, Issa)

ledger.x: 148 BC: Pharos and the towns of 219 likewise.
ledger.cp: Illyrian towns under Roman protection (Pharos, Dimale)

ledger.x: 148 BC: Gentius' three cantons south of Lissus inside the province; the Dalmatian coast north of it stays outside until Octavian (35-33).
ledger.cp: Illyria (the three cantons of Gentius' kingdom)

ledger.x: 146 BC: Corinth destroyed; Greece under Rome.
146 BC: the client state ends with its annexation (the gain above).
146 BC: 'The Thessalian League was one of the several Greek leagues the Roman tolerated until 146 BCE', when Mummius 'razed the city of Corinth to the ground, disbanded the leagues'.
146 BC: 'all leagues and other political entities were dissolved'.
146 BC: 'the Greek states were grouped into the Roman province of Macedonia'.
133 BC: Numantia razed after its capture; 'an era of lasting peace in Hispania until the Sertorian War'.
133-129 BC: Attalus III 'chose to bequeath his kingdom to Rome' (died 133); 'the pretender Eumenes III rebelled' and was captured at Stratonikeia by Perperna the following year.
129 BC: Eumenes III captured; the province organised.
116 BC: 'Western Phrygia was added in 116 BC' to Asia; after Apamea (188) it had gone to Mithridates V of Pontus.
102 BC: Marcus Antonius against the pirates.
96 BC: Ptolemy Apion 'died childless in 96 BC and left his kingdom to the Roman Republic.

ledger.cp: Marsi, Marrucini, Paeligni, Frentani and Vestini (Italian allies)

ledger.x: 91 BC: the Lucanians rebel with the Samnites ('took part with the Samnites against Rome (91 - 88 BC)', Lucanians page).
91-87 BC: the Social War's theatres: the northern 'centred on Asculum, in the lands of the Piceni and Marsi', the southern 'Samnium, Lucania, Apulia, and Campania'.
90 BC: the Etruscan and Umbrian cities become citizen communities (Lex Julia).
90 BC: the Italiote Greek cities likewise.
90 BC: 'The Umbri played a minor role in the Social War and as a result were granted citizenship in 90 BC'.
89 BC: Asculum falls; the northern theatre collapses.
89 BC: the Lex Pompeia gives Latin rights to the Transpadani; the Po valley is drawn as Roman territory from here, as the province of Cisalpine Gaul 'probably officially established' c.
89 BC: the Insubres' foedus gives way to Latin rights; 'after which the Insubres ceased to exist as a distinct people' (49).
89 BC: the Veneti likewise (Lex Pompeia de Transpadanis; Roman citizenship 49, Regio X under Augustus).
87 BC: Samnium and Lucania nominally pacified.
85 BC: Asia recovered; the Treaty of Dardanos.
78 BC: 'The third Dalmatian war 78–76 BC finished with the capture of Salona'.
77 BC: 'most of the Iberia Peninsula' under Sertorius, both Citerior and Ulterior consolidated between 80 and 77; drawn as a rebel state (rule 5, slug sertorian-hispania) hatched in its own colour.
76 BC: Salona passes to Rome ('finished with the capture of Salona'). dalmatae.json /ledger/5 books the same loss.
74 BC: the bequest's local administration ends with the province.
72 BC: the Sertorian War ends in a 'Sullan victory'.
67 BC: Zela. 'In spring 67 BC, Mithridates returned to Pontus. Roman forces under Triarius were defeated at the battle of Zela, with 7,000 Roman dead'; Lucullus 'lost nearly all of Anatolia'.
63 BC: Mithridates dies at Panticapaeum, killed at his own order by his Gallic bodyguard Bituitus after Pharnaces' revolt.

ledger.cp: Gallic tribes (Helvetii, Suebi, Belgae, Veneti, Arverni)
Gallic tribes (Helvetii, Suebi, Belgae, Veneti, Arverni)
Gallic tribes (Helvetii, Suebi, Belgae, Veneti, Arverni)

ledger.x: 56 BC: the Veneti, Armorica and Aquitania.
ledger.cp: Gallic tribes (Helvetii, Suebi, Belgae, Veneti, Arverni)
Gallic tribes (Helvetii, Suebi, Belgae, Veneti, Arverni)

ledger.x: 50 BC: 'little campaigning took place and all tribes had surrendered'; Uxellodunum (51) 'was the last major resistance'.
ledger.cp: Gallic tribes (Helvetii, Suebi, Belgae, Veneti, Arverni)

ledger.x: 48 BC: while Caesar was besieged in Alexandria Pharnaces 'seized Colchis easily', 'seize[d] Lesser Armenia, part of Cappadocia' and 'conquered the rest of Pontus'.
47 BC: Cyprus returned to the Ptolemies.
47 BC: Caesar 'defeated Pharnaces in the Battle of Zela'; Pharnaces sailed to the Bosporus and was killed there. cimmerian-bosporus.json /ledger/14.
46 BC: the Numidian client kingdom ends with Juba I; western Numidia goes to Bocchus of Mauretania and Sittius.

42 BC: Sicily held by Sextus ('42 BC – controls Sicily with a powerful navy'); drawn as rebel-held (rule 5) until Naulochus, including the peace of 39, because the Pact gave him the island only 'in exchange for keeping the grain supply to Rome open' and the war resumed (Octavian 'was defeated in the naval battle of…
40 BC: Judea's client Hyrcanus II overthrown; Pacorus 'installed Antigonus (40-37 BC)'.
40 BC: 'in 40 BC Sextus' admiral, the freedman Menas, seized Sardinia from Octavian's governor Marcus Lurius'.
40 BC: 'He captured Sardinia in 40 BC for Sextus, driving out Octavian's governor Marcus Lurius'.
38 BC: 'In 38 BC Menas surrendered Sardinia to Octavian and received equestrian rank as a reward.'
38 BC: Menas' surrender ends the contest over the islands.
37 BC: Judea again a client under Herod, who 'ousted Antigonus with Roman help in 37 BC'.
36 BC: eastern Phrygia, Lycaonia, Isauria and Pisidia to Amyntas of Galatia, a client king (tint under galatia).

September 36 BC: 'In the Battle of Naulochus, Agrippa destroyed the remainder of Sextus' fleet'; Lepidus and Statilius Taurus invaded Sicily and Sextus lost his base; he was 'captured in 35 BC, and executed without trial in Miletus'.
September 36 BC: Sicily is Octavian's again.
34 BC: 'The fourth and final conflict occurred 34–33 BC during Octavian's expedition to Illyricum'.
33 BC: 'Upon his own death in 33 BC, Bocchus II bequeathed his entire kingdom to Octavian'; 'Octavian placed Mauretania under temporary Roman administration for eight years'.
33 BC: the Roman-Dalmatae wars 'lasted until 33 BC when Octavian' installed Roman hegemony.
32 BC: the occupation lapses: 'the Romans lost hegemony during the Final War of the Roman Republic in 32-30 BC'.
32 BC: the 66 BC client relation ends: 'the Romans lost hegemony during the Final War of the Roman Republic in 32-30 BC'; in 20 BC Augustus made Armenia 'a buffer zone between the two major powers'.

wars.name: Latin War
wars.outcome: 'Roman victory, dissolution of Latin League' (338): some Latin towns Romanised, others municipia, some colonies; Capua's civitas sine suffragio.

wars.name: Samnite Wars
wars.outcome: First (343-341), Second (326-304) and Third (298-290) Samnite Wars: 'Roman control over much of central Italy and part of southern Italy'; Samnium allied, the Sabines annexed, the Aequi crushed.

wars.name: Pyrrhic War
wars.outcome: 'Carthago-Roman victory' (281-275 infobox); Tarentum fell in 272, the Italiote cities 'quickly sought terms'; Rome's hegemony over Italy complete; colonies at Paestum (273), Beneventum (268), Aesernia (263).

wars.name: Roman–Etruscan Wars (late phase)
wars.outcome: Roman victories at Lake Vadimo; Caere taken 273 ('Brice's proposed end'), Volsinii destroyed 264 ('Last Etruscan resistance crushed'); Falerii's revolt of 241 'a last gasp'.

wars.name: First Punic War
wars.outcome: 'Roman victory'; 'Roman annexation of Sicily (except Syracuse)'; Carthage evacuated Sicily and paid 3,200 talents; Sardinia and Corsica ceded in 238/237.

wars.name: Ligurian Wars
wars.outcome: 'Ti. Sempronius Gracchus fought them in 238 BC'; in 180 about 40,000 Apuani were deported; 'M. Claudius Marcellus drove back the Apuani for the last time in 155 BC'. No transfer of land is dated on the page.

wars.name: Illyrian Wars
wars.outcome: First (229-228): protectorate over the Greek towns; Second (220-219): Demetrius fled, Pharos dismantled; Third (168): Gentius beaten at Scodra, Illyria split into three cantons.

wars.name: Gallic War of 225–222 BC (Telamon, Clastidium)
wars.outcome: Telamon (225): the Celtic army 'caught between two Roman forces and destroyed'; the Boii submit by treaty; Mediolanum falls and the Insubres surrender (222).

wars.name: Second Punic War
wars.outcome: 'Roman victory'; 'Roman conquest of Carthaginian Iberia; Carthaginian African territories reduced'; peace of spring 201.

wars.name: First Macedonian War
wars.outcome: Infobox 'stalemate and Peace of Phoenice' (205); 'There were no decisive engagements'; Aetolian treaty of 211 ('the Aetolians would conduct operations on land, the Romans at sea'); Attalus took Aegina.

wars.name: Roman reconquest of Cisalpine Gaul
wars.outcome: The Insubres submitted in 197 and were bound by a foedus; 'Scipio Nasica completed the conquest of the Boii' in 191; colonies at Bononia (189), Mutina and Parma (183), Aquileia (181).

wars.name: Second Macedonian War
wars.outcome: Infobox 'March 200 - June 197 BC', 'Roman coalition victory'; 'Philip had to remove all his garrisons in Greek cities in Europe and Asia' and pay 1,000 talents; 'Freedom of the Greeks' proclaimed at the Isthmian Games of May 196; Roman garrisons in Corinth…

wars.name: Roman–Seleucid War (Aetolian phase)
wars.outcome: Infobox 192-188 BC: 'Pergamon annexes Lydia, Phrygia, Mysia, Pisidia and Pamphylia from Seleucid Empire', 'Rhodes annexes Caria and Lycia', 'Aetolian League becomes subject to Rome'; Rome itself gained no land in Asia (the '(Allegiance of Seleucid Empire to…

wars.name: Celtiberian and Numantine Wars
wars.outcome: Gracchus' pacification (182-179); the revolt of 154-151; the Numantine War (143-133) ending with Numantia razed: 'Expansion of the Roman territory through Celtiberia'.

wars.name: Lusitanian War
wars.outcome: Galba's massacre; Viriathus' victories from 148; his assassination under Caepio and the Lusitanians 'became Roman subjects'.

wars.name: Third Macedonian War
wars.outcome: 'Roman victory'; 'Macedon divided into four merides (Amphipolis, Thessalonica, Pella, and Pelagonia)'; Epirus' seventy cities sacked and 150,000 enslaved; Illyria split into three cantons.

wars.name: Fourth Macedonian War and Achaean War
wars.outcome: Andriscus defeated near Pydna (148) and the province of Macedonia created; Mummius destroyed Corinth (146); Athens and Sparta free; Greece's formal status disputed.

wars.name: Third Punic War
wars.outcome: 'Roman victory; Destruction of Carthage'; the former Carthaginian territories annexed as the province of Africa with Utica as capital.

wars.name: Revolt of Eumenes III (Aristonicus)
wars.outcome: Perperna defeated and captured Eumenes at Stratonikeia; Aquillius organised the province of Asia (129).

wars.name: First Transalpine War
wars.outcome: Fabius Maximus defeated the Allobroges and Arverni at the Isère; 'The area became a Roman province in 121 BC'; Narbo founded 118.

wars.name: Cimbrian War
wars.outcome: Infobox '6 October 113-101 BC', 'Roman victory'; the Cimbri 'invaded the Roman province of Gallia Narbonensis' in 109 and Catulus withdrew behind the Po, 'leaving the countryside open to the invaders'; Arausio 105, Aquae Sextiae 102, Vercellae 101.

wars.name: Jugurthine War
wars.outcome: Jugurtha defeated; 'his former territory passed to the Mauritanian king Bocchus I' (Africa page): no Roman gain.

wars.name: Social War
wars.outcome: 'Roman victory'; citizenship conceded by the Lex Julia (90) and Lex Plautia Papiria (89); Asculum fell November 89, Silo killed 88, the Samnites and Lucanians 'nominally pacified in 87 BC'.

wars.name: First Mithridatic War
wars.outcome: 'Roman victory'; 'Return to status quo ante bellum (treaty of Dardanus)': Mithridates surrendered his conquests and kept Pontus; the Senate never ratified the treaty.

wars.name: Sulla's civil wars
wars.outcome: Sulla marched on Rome in 88, seized the city in 83 and was dictator from November 82 (Roman Republic page); the Colline Gate (82) ended the Samnites as a people (Samnites page).

wars.name: Second Mithridatic War
wars.outcome: Infobox '83-81 BC', 'Pontic victory', territorial changes 'None, Mithridates left in possession of Pontus'; 'Mithridates drove all the Roman garrisons out of Cappadocia', and Ariobarzanes 'was to retain the part of Cappadocia he held at the time'.

wars.name: Sertorian War
wars.outcome: 'Sullan victory'; Sertorius murdered by Perperna (72), Perperna executed by Pompey; Hispania recovered.

wars.name: Dalmatian Wars (third and fourth)
wars.outcome: 'The third Dalmatian war 78–76 BC finished with the capture of Salona'; 'The fourth and final conflict occurred 34–33 BC during Octavian's expedition to Illyricum'; the wars 'lasted until 33 BC when Octavian' installed Roman hegemony.

wars.name: Third Mithridatic War
wars.outcome: 'Roman victory'; 'Pontus and Syria become Roman provinces', Judea a client, Armenia an ally; Mithridates dead at Panticapaeum (63).

wars.name: Cretan War of Metellus
wars.outcome: Crete conquered after a three-year campaign; united with Cyrenaica as one province (67 per the page, which also says 66).

wars.name: Pompey's pirate war
wars.outcome: Korakesion 'brought Cilicia Trachea under Roman control'; the province reorganised in 64.

wars.name: Gallic Wars
wars.outcome: 'Roman victory'; 'Gaul conquered by Roman Republic'; Alesia (52), Uxellodunum (51); provinces organised under Augustus in 27.

wars.name: Caesar's civil war
wars.outcome: 'Caesarian victory' (10 January 49 to 17 March 45); Massilia lost its independence (49), Cyprus returned to Cleopatra (47), Juba's Numidia became Africa Nova (46).

wars.name: Caesar's war against Pharnaces II
wars.outcome: Pharnaces 'conquered the rest of Pontus' while Caesar was in Alexandria; Caesar 'defeated Pharnaces in the Battle of Zela' (47); Pharnaces died that year in the Bosporus.

wars.name: Liberators' civil war
wars.outcome: Infobox '43-42 BC', 'Triumvir victory, Destruction of Liberators ...

wars.name: Sicilian War against Sextus Pompey
wars.outcome: Pact of Misenum 39 ('Pompey was given legitimate control over Sicily and Sardinia in exchange for keeping the grain supply to Rome open'); the war resumed; 'In the Battle of Naulochus, Agrippa destroyed the remainder of Sextus' fleet' (36); Sextus captured…

wars.name: Parthian invasion of Syria
wars.outcome: Pacorus and Labienus overran Syria (40); Ventidius destroyed the Parthian army and killed Pacorus (38); Herod retook Jerusalem (37).

wars.name: War of Actium
wars.outcome: Actium, 2 September 31; Octavian's victory led to the title Augustus (16 January 27) and the end of the Republic; 'resulting in Octavian gaining control of all of Egypt and Cyprus' (Roman Cyprus page), Egypt 'seized by Octavian as his personal possession' in…

certainty.note: Ancient frontiers throughout: Italy's allied communities had treaty boundaries but no surveyed line; the provinces' edges (the Hebrus for Macedonia, the fossa regia for Africa, the Rhine for Gaul) are the sharp exceptions; the Ebro of 226…
